episodes.title: The AI Wealth Problem
episodes.about: Anthropic's plan to devote billions to public benefit raises a bigger question: who gets to decide how AI wealth is shared? NLW explores the collision between philanthropy, concentrated power, and democratic accountability. In the headlines: OpenCode's major security breach, mounting AI bubble fears, and Microsoft's canceled UK data center deal.
episodes.why: Anthropic is pledging billions to public benefit: NLW asks who decides how AI wealth gets shared, plus OpenCode's security breach, Microsoft's canceled UK data center, and the latest AI bubble fears.

episodes.title: What Happens When Everyone Has a Health Expert in Their Pocket? | OpenAI’s Karan Singhal
episodes.about: More than 300 million people use ChatGPT for health and wellness questions each week. OpenAI's Karan Singhal explains why OpenAI trains healthcare expertise directly into its general-purpose frontier models, how it works with hundreds of medical experts to evaluate safety and disagreement, and why the company sees AI as a complement to doctors rather than a replacement. They also discuss integrations with Epic, AI copilots for clinicians, and personal agents navigating appointments and health records.
episodes.why: Out today: 300 million people already ask ChatGPT health questions every week - OpenAI's health lead on training medical expertise into the frontier models, evaluating safety with doctors, and agents that book the appointment too.

episodes.title: Inside the Robot Data Factory: Mecka's Josh Gao on Sensorizing Humans to Train Robots
episodes.about: Robotics never got the internet's gift of free training data, so someone has to manufacture it. Josh Gao, founder and CEO of Mecka AI, runs one of the largest robot data factories: custom baseball caps and tactile gloves because nothing off the shelf captures force, 100-gigabit upload lines to move hundreds of petabytes, and custom quality gates. He lays out the training recipe the industry is converging on - roughly a million hours of egocentric human data, tens of thousands of hours of robot data, and a few hours of in-domain teleoperation - and argues the field is still orders of magnitude behind Tesla's FSD, so there will be no single GPT-3 moment for robotics, just a steady unlock of commercial tasks.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Sequoia's show for AI builders: robots have no internet to train on, so Mecka manufactures the data with sensor caps and tactile gloves, and Gao explains why robotics gets no GPT-3 moment, only steady unlocks.

episodes.title: 20VC: Horizontal vs Vertical Agents: Who Wins | Model Routing: Commodity or Increasing in Value | The Future of the Inference Market | Why Founders Should Take Discounts for Tier 1 Firms with Harrison Chase, LangChain
episodes.about: Harrison Chase is the co-founder and CEO of LangChain, which helps developers build, test and deploy AI agents; LangChain works with 35% of the Fortune 500, has passed a billion open-source downloads, and processes over a billion events daily through LangSmith. The memo covers why it is still so hard to build AI agents, whether the model labs will eat the agent stack, whether model routing is a real business or a commodity, why no one has solved AI memory, and why AI bills are exploding as tokens get cheaper.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Harry Stebbings' venture show, in memo format: LangChain's Harrison Chase on horizontal vs vertical agents, model routing as business or commodity, unsolved AI memory, and AI bills rising while tokens get cheaper.

episodes.title: Don Wilson on the GPU Market's Trillion Dollar Question
episodes.about: When DRW founder and CEO Don Wilson spoke to Odd Lots in Chicago last year, he said he wanted to build a market for GPUs that would eventually be bigger than oil. Recorded live at City Winery, he returns to talk about what has changed: DRW's 'crunch spread' (the GPU version of a crack spread), the latest on plans to launch GPU futures, and his take on the recent tech selloff, including credit concerns around neocloud CoreWeave.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Bloomberg's markets show: DRW's Don Wilson is building GPU futures and a GPU 'crunch spread' to make compute trade like oil, and he weighs the tech selloff and CoreWeave's credit.
